publisher: U.S. Census Bureau (America Counts story, with AmeriCorps)
table: Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement, hours served by formal volunteers
title: New U.S. Census Bureau and AmeriCorps Research Tracks Virtual Volunteering for First Time (Laura Hanson Schlachter and Tim Marshall, November 19, 2024)
universe: Formal volunteers age 16 and over (people who volunteered through an organization in the past year)
limits: Hours per formal volunteer in a year, through any organization, not only causes; the mean is pulled up by a few very active volunteers, so the median is the better check on a typical volunteer. National only. Read through the fetch tool; the AmeriCorps PDF of the same report returns 403 from the cloud. Total hours over volunteers (4.99 billion over 75.7 million) gives 65.9, not the story's 70; the story's averages are its own published estimates, kept as given.
quotes: Over 75.7 million or 28.3% of the U.S. population age 16 and up formally volunteered through an organization
formal volunteers served an estimated 4.99 billion hours
average hours served per volunteer in the previous year dropped from 96.5 hours when the CEV began in 2017 to 70 hours in 2023.
Similarly, half of formal volunteers served 40 hours in 2017 compared to 24 hours in the latest data.
use: Set beside a played town's cause volunteers by the cause-activity year report (scripts/research/cause-activity-year.ts): hours volunteered a year by each person who volunteered for a cause (their volunteer acts times volunteerHours), beside the hours of real formal volunteers through any organization, median 24 to 40 and mean 70 to 96.5. The survey's volunteers are over a quarter of people and count every organization, so it is an exploratory proxy, not a band for cause volunteering. Never a cap; a holder's own time, money and pulls decide each act.
